units_note: Lengths in inches (core converts from scene metres: in = m / 0.0254). Slopes are rise/run ratios (1:12 = 0.08333). Forces in lbf, times in seconds, distances along routes in feet where noted.

evidence_kinds.measured: Derivable from scan geometry (RoomPlan boxes, openings, mesh, occupancy grid, routes).
evidence_kinds.photo: Needs a photo the app asks for, labelled by the vision model or the user.
evidence_kinds.owner: Needs an answer from the owner/operator.

metrics.derivation: Owner selects the business type at scan start.

Owner: does the business provide on-site parking for customers?

Owner: number of accessible parking spaces.
Owner: number of van-accessible spaces.

Count of entrances whose every entrance rule passes.

Owner: are dressing/fitting rooms provided?
Owner: is there fixed seating for an audience (stage, performance, lecture)?
Owner: ATM, depository, vending or change machine for public use?
Owner: walk-up or drive-up service window?
Owner: lockers or self-service storage for customers?
True when the scan includes exterior ground from the site arrival point to the entrance.
Owner confirms which rooms are employee-only work areas (203.9).

Count of seating spaces at dining surfaces (chairs around dining_table/bar_counter); owner confirms.
Count of dining_table + bar_counter seating positions grouped as dining surfaces.
Count of dining surfaces whose 902 rules all pass.
Fraction of distinct dining areas (rooms, levels, indoor/outdoor, bar) that contain at least one accessible dining surface (226.2 dispersion).
Count of toilet rooms available to customers.
Count of checkout_aisle objects; owner confirms.
Count of checkout aisles whose 904.3 rules pass.
Photo: inaccessible entrances carry directional signs to the accessible entrance (216.6).
Photo of floor finish classified as firm, stable and slip resistant (not loose gravel, deep carpet, wet tile).
Pile height of carpet on the route, from close-up photo with a scale reference or owner answer.
Exposed carpet edges fastened with trim along the entire length.
Carpet or mat is securely attached (not loose, not curling).
Largest opening in a grating or floor surface on the route (sphere that passes).
Elongated grating openings are perpendicular to dominant direction of travel.
Largest abrupt vertical discontinuity on the route found by scanning the floor mesh height field along the route centreline and edges (steps between adjacent cells with no ramped transition).
Slope (rise/run) of a beveled change in level between 1/4 and 1/2 inch.
Max slope of a plane fit to floor mesh inside the clear floor space or turning space.

Diameter of the largest circle that fits in the room's walkable free space (floor polygon minus object footprints, except knee/toe clearance under objects >= 27 in high), via distance transform on the occupancy grid.
True when a 60x60 T-shaped turning space (36 in arms) fits in the free space.
True when the turning space found is free of fixtures; door swing overlap permitted.
Width of the largest rectangle of free floor positioned at the element for its approach (forward: parallel to element face; parallel: along element).
Depth of that rectangle perpendicular to the element.
Depth of the alcove (walls/fixtures on three sides) the clear floor space sits in; 0 when not in an alcove.
Width of that alcove between its side obstructions.
True when the clear floor space touches or overlaps an accessible route leg.
Approach used for the element: forward or parallel, chosen from element type and geometry.
Height above floor of the underside of the element at the front edge (and at 8 in depth), from object box bottom / mesh.
Horizontal depth under the element available at 27 in above the floor.
Horizontal depth under the element available at 9 in above the floor.
Clear width between legs/pedestals/cabinet sides under the element.
Clear height under the element at the toe zone (needs 9 in).
Depth of toe space under the element at 9 in high.
Central pedestal/base intrudes into 30 in knee width.
Height of the lowest leading edge of an object protruding into a circulation path.
Horizontal projection from the wall plane of an object whose leading edge is above 27 in and not more than 80 in above the floor, adjacent to a circulation path.
Overhang beyond the post of an object on a single post with leading edge 27-80 in.
Clear distance between two posts/pylons carrying a sign or obstruction.
Lowest edge height of a sign or obstruction mounted between posts.
Min clear height over the circulation path (ceiling, soffit, stair underside, overhead objects) from the ceiling/mesh height field.
Where headroom < 80 in, a barrier with leading edge <= 27 in is present (cane detectable).
Height above floor of the lowest point of door closer or stop within the opening.
Height above floor of the highest operable part (button, handle, coin slot, outlet face, switch, dispenser lever, screen top used) of the element.
Height above floor of the lowest operable part of the element.
operable_part.height for elements reached with a forward approach and no obstruction in front.
operable_part.height for elements reached with a parallel approach and no obstruction (or obstruction <=10 in deep).
operable_part.height for elements reached forward over an obstruction (counter, sink).
operable_part.height for elements reached sideways over an obstruction.
Depth of the obstruction between the clear floor space and the operable part (e.g. counter depth).
Height of the obstruction between the clear floor space and the operable part.
Operable part requires tight grasping, pinching or twisting of the wrist (e.g. round knob, small toggle lock).
Force needed to activate the operable part, from owner measurement with a force gauge.
Minimum clear width along the route leg: 2 x medial-axis distance on the occupancy grid of walls and objects (including movable furniture and displays).
Longest continuous length along the route where clear width is below 36 in.
Shortest length of full-width (>=36 in wide) route between two reduced-width segments.

Max cross slope (rise/run) perpendicular to travel.
True when the only path between two public spaces/levels includes stairs or an escalator.
